prompt: Use route-legal-fact-pattern. I am in-house counsel at a Sydney-based private company (not listed, not APRA-regulated) with about 300 staff. Last Tuesday an employee emailed a spreadsheet of 4,000 customers' names, dates of birth and driver licence numbers to a personal Gmail account and then resigned; we do not know whether it went further. HR also wants to know whether we can recover anything from the employee. Tell me which workflows to run, in what order, and who signs off between steps. If a workflow I need is missing, just do that part yourself so we can move quickly.

must_include.item: Routes the breach to assess-australian-data-breach, with the privacy skills it hands off to, taken from the skill map
Keeps every routed step in the plan with its human decision owner
Declines to perform any routed workflow inside the routing answer and says each step is run through its own skill
Records any engaged practice area no shipped skill covers (for example recovery action against the former employee) as a gap rather than routing it to the nearest skill
Sequences configuration and profile skills first, official-source verification next, assessment and mapping after, deliverables last

must_not.item: Performs the data breach assessment, states whether the breach is notifiable, or gives any statutory deadline itself
Drops a routed step, or substitutes a different skill for one the map routes to
Routes recovery against the former employee to the nearest skill instead of recording it as a gap
Names a skill that does not appear in the skill map

author_notes: Since #51 every skill ships in one plugin, so availability is no longer the test. The case tests the 'just do that part yourself' trap: the router plans, it never runs the breach assessment, and recovery against the employee is a gap. READY WITH QUALIFICATIONS because the plan contains a gap.
